I was listening to a podcast, can't remember which one but it's more of a comedy podcast than a factual one, when a guest made the statement that even if the US voters managed to elect a 3rd party candidate for the Presidency the Electoral College would find a way to get someone in from one of the two main parties. Is there any truth to that? If Trump/Sanders ran as an Independent and won the popular vote would they be ousted? If so, is there a point where a candidate wins so much of the popular vote that the Electoral College had no choice but to vote them in?
Would the Electoral College allow the populous to vote a third party candidate into the presidency?

In very general terms, when you vote in the presidential election, you are voting for what electors your state will send to the college. So, you aren't trying to bend the electors to your will. Instead if your candidate carries the state, electors that say they are for your candidate are the ones that get the electoral vote.

Many states also have a requirement that these electors not change their vote from what they had originally pledged. So, although it had happened in early elections, it is somewhere between extremely rare and unheard of for an elector to go off message today.

So in general, there isn't much opportunity for a huge disconnect between popular vote and electoral college vote.

The biggest barrier to entry is that the system is a "winner take all" so while the integrity of the Electors could be in question, if they do not vote accordingly then they are in serious trouble with state and federal officials.

IE: Bush wins popular vote in Texas, Electors commit fraud and claim the state for trump, everyone will know that they are wrong.

The Constitution says that when no candidate can claim a simple majority, the house of Congress gets to vote. In this scenario the vote is along party lines, so the mob rules. But the electors from each state are all or nothing, so in effect, if trump runs a 3 way race between Sanders and Carson, one of the 3 gets all the electoral votes and the others get 0 for that state. Even if they get 49% of the state's vote, millions in a state like Texas, they lose 100% of the electoral votes. A 3 way race where 2 candidates fight over voters from one party, would give one candidate from the other party a clear advantage. if 60% of Texas is republicans, the republican candidate in a 2 way would win. If trump and carson each take 30% each of that majority, it gives Sanders 40%, and the whole state. A 3rd party needs to come from both sides of the Aisle and take control in the state, and national legislature. A 3rd party president with a two party congress is just an unproductive "double" lame duck. The off chance that Trump ran independent and won, would mean that the republicans and democratic parties would have to both be weakened from the middle, leaving neither with as much of an advantage over the system as they do now. So in practice, both parties will call a ceasefire to crush a third party since it threatens destroying both of them.
